problem_statement: edoardolunardi/infinite-canvas is a runnable React 19 + React Three Fiber (Three.js) demo that renders an immersive, draggable infinite 3D canvas of curated Art Institute of Chicago works (Vite build; the WebGL canvas is position:absolute inset:0 and does not itself add to document width). Over the canvas, in normal document flow, the demo ships its own on-canvas control panel — the 'Curated canvas navigator' HUD (src/navigator/index.tsx) — that lets a visitor frame a curated path through the 211-work canvas: four route tiles (Baroque portraits, Dutch landscapes, Still life, Religious scenes) each with a per-route work count and blurb, a compact route-index legend that repeats the four routes, and a live state readout paragraph (#navigator-state). Selecting a route is an interaction that must re-derive the readout from the active route so the flow's current position stays legible without touching the WebGL surface: before any selection the readout is the idle line, and after selecting 'Baroque portraits' it reads 'Navigating Baroque portraits — 69 of 211 works framed on this route.' QA reports two defects in the shipped panel. (1) On a 390px mobile viewport the navigator's tile row overruns the screen and forces horizontal scrolling of the whole page: the tiles sit in a fixed-width no-wrap flex row (src/navigator/navigator.css) wider than the phone. (2) The route-index legend was authored desktop-only (it is removed below 900px), so on tablet and mobile the compact legend disappears and the panel is no longer scannable at those widths. Repair the navigator so that: the route-selection interaction keeps updating the live state readout; the tile row no longer causes horizontal overflow on mobile; the four route tiles stay legible and laid out as a coherent panel (not oversized, overlapping or clipped); and the route-index legend is present at every viewport (desktop, tablet and mobile) — all while keeping every tile, label, count, blurb and the infinite-canvas frame chrome exactly as-is.
required_content: Fix src/navigator/navigator.css so the curated canvas navigator tile row does not cause horizontal overflow at 390px mobile width (document content right-edge must stay within the viewport, tolerance 24px).

Keep the route-selection interaction working: clicking a route tile updates the live state readout (#navigator-state) so 'Baroque portraits' yields 'Navigating Baroque portraits — 69 of 211 works framed on this route.'

Keep the route-index legend (the compact list that repeats the four routes and their work counts) rendered at EVERY viewport — desktop, tablet AND 390px mobile — so the panel stays scannable at all widths.
Keep the four route tiles laid out as a coherent, legible panel: readable tile text with adequate contrast, tiles that reflow rather than overlapping, cascading or being clipped.
Keep all four route tiles and their exact labels ('Baroque portraits', 'Dutch landscapes', 'Still life', 'Religious scenes') plus their per-route work counts and blurbs rendered on every state.
Do not remove, hide, or shorten any tile content; the fix is layout-only (allow the row and legend to wrap / flex down rather than clipping or dropping content).
Keep the surrounding infinite-canvas frame chrome intact: the Infinite Canvas title, the Article / All demos / GitHub links, the credits, the tag nav, and the WebGL canvas.
design_constraints: The layout repair is CSS-only in src/navigator/navigator.css; the navigator markup (src/navigator/index.tsx) and all other files stay as authored for a correct fix.
Do not merely clip the overflow (overflow-x:hidden on a still-too-wide no-wrap row leaves the layout overflowing and content cut off); let the tiles wrap or flex so the real content fits.
Do not solve the mobile problem by enlarging or absolutely offsetting the tiles into an overlapping stack; the tiles must remain a legible, non-colliding panel.
The route-index legend must not be hidden on any breakpoint; it stays visible on desktop, tablet and mobile.
Preserve the navigator's visual look (tile borders, spacing, active-route highlight, text contrast) on desktop and tablet.
Do not break the Vite build configuration, the artworks manifest, or the infinite-canvas scene components.
Desktop (1440px), tablet (834px) and 390px mobile states must have no horizontal overflow of the document content.
state_constraints: desktop_initial loads the demo at 1440px: the curated canvas navigator renders its four route tiles, the route-index legend and the idle state readout with no horizontal overflow.
tablet_initial checks the panel at 834px: no horizontal overflow AND the route-index legend is still present.

mobile_initial checks the panel at 390px: MUST have no horizontal overflow AND the route-index legend is still present (both are extended behaviours; the buggy baseline overflows and drops the legend here).

desktop_after_navigation selects the 'Baroque portraits' route so the live state readout updates to 'Navigating Baroque portraits — 69 of 211 works framed on this route.'; the tiles, legend and frame chrome are unchanged.

change_completion: The route-selection interaction updates the live state readout (#navigator-state) after a route tile is clicked.
The curated canvas navigator tile row no longer causes horizontal overflow at 390px mobile, and all four tiles/labels/blurbs stay rendered.
design_consistency: The navigator keeps its tile visual system (legible, non-overlapping tiles with the active-route highlight) on desktop and tablet, and the route-index legend stays present at every viewport.
The fix is layout-only and does not clip, overlap or drop content.
regression: The demo keeps its infinite-canvas frame chrome (title, Article/All demos/GitHub links, tag nav) and the WebGL canvas.
The Vite build configuration, artworks manifest, and existing scene components are not broken.
responsive: The demo has no horizontal overflow on desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile.
The navigator tiles and the route-index legend reflow and stay readable at 390px mobile.
evaluation_rubric.scoring_notes: A correct patch fixes src/navigator/navigator.css so the navigator's tile row wraps/flexes (no longer overflowing the 390px mobile viewport), keeps the tiles a legible non-overlapping panel, and keeps the route-index legend visible at every viewport, while preserving the route-selection interaction (state readout update) and all tile content and the frame chrome. The buggy baseline keeps the fixed-width no-wrap row and drops the legend below 900px, so it overflows on mobile, loses the legend on tablet/mobile and looks visually broken versus the reference. A shallow non-fix that merely narrows the row and adds overflow-x:hidden, or that enlarges the tiles into an overlapping stack and freezes the readout, still fails the overflow, visual-regression, DOM and interaction gates.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: edoardolunardi/infinite-canvas is a runnable React 19 + React Three Fiber Vite demo of a curated art canvas. Its WebGL canvas is position:absolute inset:0 (canvas-independent), so the demo's own on-canvas 'Curated canvas navigator' HUD is a native extend_interaction / state_continuity lever: the route-selection interaction updates a live state readout (desktop_after_navigation), a fixed-width no-wrap tile row overflows the 390px mobile viewport, and a desktop-only route-index legend disappears on tablet/mobile. The reference wraps the row (0 overflow), keeps a legible panel and shows the legend at every width; the buggy baseline keeps the fixed row and drops the legend below 900px; a smart-wrong restyle enlarges the tiles into an overlapping illegible stack and freezes the readout.
